summary: Midgard's history as its loremasters tell it: the realm's own chronicles where they speak, the old Norse songs beside them, and the loremasters' own telling where both are silent.

eras.name: The Age of Ice
eras.summary: Before the gods set the world in order: the rime giants, a dragon dying in the northern ice, things frozen that are still frozen.

events.text: In Norse myth the rime-giants (hrimthursar) descend from Bergelmir, who alone survived the flood of Ymir's blood.
In Norse myth the primeval cow Audhumla fed Ymir and licked the first of the gods out of the ice.
A dragon died in the ice of Aegir long before any people came; Kula later raised Tuscaran's citadel on its bones.
Fornfrusenen was frozen into the north wall of the glacier in this age, and the bones of Modernagrav were buried.

eras.name: The Age of the Troll Fathers
eras.summary: The ancient precursors of trolls and kobolds dig Trollheim under Aegir and give their dead to the mound at its root; the iarn dwarves already live in the iron wood beside the old one.

events.text: Troll and kobold myths tell of the Troll Fathers, wise precursors of both races, who lived in Trollheim on the island of Aegir.
The Troll Fathers raised a mound of the dead under Trollheim's last hall; Nosdoden later lay down on it.
Iarnvidiur, the old one of the Iarnwood, was on Aegir before the iarn dwarf clans; Mahattava's lake was older still.

eras.name: The Binding of the Wolf
eras.summary: The gods bind Fenrir and Loki. Before the chain closes, the wolf's daughter flies south to Malmohus; his brood runs in the Iron Wood; a splinter of the sun lies in Raumarik's snow.

events.text: In Norse myth the gods bind the wolf Fenrir with the fetter Gleipnir until Ragnarok, and bind Loki under a serpent's dripping venom.
In Norse myth an old giantess in the Iron Wood breeds Fenrir's wolf-kin, among them the wolves who chase the sun and moon.
Gjalpinulva's own taunts name an aunt who keeps a place in Niflheim for her victims; Midgard's tavern talk calls her the Fenris wolf's daughter.
The quest 'The Legend of Fenrir's Folly' sends the realm's young to win a sun fragment back from the Raumarik Revenant.
A young svartalf scout told Midgard's hunters that Gjalpinulva of Malmohus was fathered by Fenris Wolf on a huge creature no one could name, and that she made the drakulv out of loneliness.
events.source: http://www.camelotherald.com/more/193.php (Camelot Herald, 2002-02-07, 1.45 patch notes; the same text first ran in the Pendragon notes, http://www.camelotherald.com/more/177.php, 2002-01-29; Wayback capture 2005-12-20)

eras.name: The Age of the Jarls
eras.summary: The old kingdoms of Midgard: jarls on the frontier hills, the Cursed Tomb sealed, tomte driven underground, the vendo in their caves, and the mine of Dodens Gruva breaking into the hall below.

events.text: Sigmund and his son Sinfjötli put on wolf-skins that they cannot take off for ten days, and live as wolves in the forest; Sinfjötli later dies of poison given by his stepmother Borghild.
Hervor's father Angantyr and his eleven brothers, the berserk sons of Arngrim, fall on Samsey to Hjalmar and Orvar-Odd; Hjorvard, Hervard and Hrani are among the brothers.
Dodens Gruva lay on the old Jamtland frontier east of Glenlock Faste, and was lost when the frontier was remade.
The Cursed Tomb holds the dishonoured warriors and kings whom the gods would not admit to Valhalla.
Summoner's Hall connects the lands of the three realms; Midgard reaches it from Dodens Gruva.
Jarl Ormarr's miners broke into the Summoner's Hall and their spiritmaster Aros bound them to the mine.
Jordheim grew from a village of heroes over the caves Relder Autansonn found; its founder lies there in his rebuilt longboat.
The houses of the gods were given two temple halls in Jordheim, a street apart, by an old peace over Loki's house.
The four pieces of the Grenlock crest were kept by Svan's sons and are made whole by Sinyr at the dverge forge in Muspelheim (Anrid's 'Grenlock Clan').
Svan's sons are the Alfevsons: Siv and Coplin, spirits; Ove, a werewolf of Askheim; Gunnar, a shade in Muspelheim.

Many generations ago the svartalf king and queen died suddenly, leaving twin princes, Hauk and Enar, and no one knew which was the firstborn. A human stranger, held for trespass, proposed a contest of arms and of magic-making in exchange for his freedom, then sabotaged Enar's artifact, laid the blame on Hauk and vanished with the kingdom's treasured artifacts.
events.source: http://www.camelotherald.com/more/1131.shtml (Camelot Herald, 2003-10-23, 'Trials of Atlantis, an Overview'; Wayback capture 2005-12-26)

events.text: Hauk left with a few followers and settled in Niflheim, a land of darkness, hard frost and freezing fog at the very bottom of the world; Enar ruled, remorseful, but Hauk would not return. Hauk's descendants are the frostalfs.
events.source: http://www.camelotherald.com/more/1131.shtml (Camelot Herald, 2003-10-23, 'Trials of Atlantis, an Overview'; Wayback capture 2005-12-26)

events.text: Sigurd, the son of Sigmund, has the sword Gram reforged from his father's broken blade by the smith Regin, and kills the dragon Fafnir by digging a pit in the path and thrusting the sword up into it as it crosses.
events.source: Volsunga saga, chapters 15 and 18; Fafnismal (Poetic Edda)

events.text: Fafnir tells the dying Sigurd that the gold carries a curse; Sigurd tastes the dragon's heart-blood while roasting it, understands the speech of birds, and kills the treacherous Regin.
Midgard's dragon-hunters still dig a second pit, because the old man at the crossing told Sigurd to; in Malmohus the hunters say the same of Gjalpinulva.

Ragnar wins Thora Town-Hart, daughter of Jarl Herraud of Gautland, by killing the lindworm that has grown around her bower, wearing shaggy trousers coated in tar and sand, and earns the name Lodbrok (Hairy-Breeches).
events.source: Ragnars saga lodbrokar (the winning of Thora)

events.text: Ragnar is captured by King Aella of Northumbria and thrown into a pit of snakes; in the saga he says from the pit that the little pigs would grunt if they knew how the old boar suffers, and his death-song, the Krakumal, lists his battles and ends that he will die laughing.
events.source: Ragnars saga lodbrokar (the snake pit) for the little pigs; Krakumal for the battle-list and the laughing death

events.text: The Krakumal's last stanzas end with the hope of drinking ale from curved horns in Odin's hall.
events.source: Krakumal (the Death-Song of Lodbrok), the closing stanzas

events.text: Hervor, the daughter of Angantyr, disguises herself as a man named Hervard, goes alone to the island of Samsey at sunset, and wakes the dead sons of Arngrim in their burial mounds, calling them by name: Hervard, the uncle who shares her borrowed name, Hjorvard, Hrani and her father Angantyr.
events.source: Hervarar saga ok Heidreks; The Waking of Angantyr (Hervararkvida)

events.text: Angantyr warns Hervor that the sword Tyrfing kills a man whenever it is drawn and will destroy her kin, but gives it to her when she curses the barrow-dead to rot in their mounds.
events.source: Hervarar saga ok Heidreks; The Waking of Angantyr (Hervararkvida)

events.text: Told of the raider-king's death in the snake pit, his sons each betray it: Björn Ironside grips his spear until the shaft keeps the print of his hand, Hvitserk squeezes a playing-piece until blood starts from his nails, Snake-in-the-Eye cuts to the bone paring his nails, and Ivar the Boneless asks how his father died and changes colour. Ivar asks Aella for as much land as an ox-hide covers, cuts the hide into strips to enclose a stronghold, and wins Aella's men from him; the brothers take Aella and carve the eagle on his back.

Starkad, a warrior of giant stock, is given three lifetimes and victory in every battle by Odin, and Thor answers each gift with a curse, among them a nithing's deed in each lifetime. Chosen by lot for Odin in a storm, his king Vikar is hanged by him in what was meant as a mock sacrifice, with a calf's gut for a noose and a reed for a spear, which turn into a rope and a spear as he strikes.
events.source: Gautreks saga (public domain); Saxo Grammaticus, Gesta Danorum, also tells of Vikar hanged for the gods

events.text: In his old age Starkad, who killed King Olo for gold and repented of it, hangs the gold round his neck to pay the man who will kill him rather than die in his bed; Hather, whose father he had slain, takes the gold and strikes off his head, and the head bites the earth as it falls.

Beowulf of the Geats tears the arm from Grendel of the giant-kin in the Danish king's hall, follows Grendel's mother down into her mere and kills her with a giant-made sword whose blade melts in her blood, rules the Geats for fifty winters, and dies in his old age killing a dragon.

The grandmothers of Gotar keep Beowulf's song and the winning of Thora as the two old songs of the Gautar; the Cursed Tomb's tellers argue Starkad's place; Varulvhamn's wolfaur sing the Volsungs' wolf-skins; Svarhamr's furs are called the hairy breeches; Vasudheim's skalds sing Ivar and the cow Sibilja; Jordheim's skalds sing the founders beside Starkad and the raider-king's sons.

eras.name: The War of the Realms
eras.summary: After Arthur's death the three realms go to war. Keeps rise on the frontiers, the Glacier Giant throws all comers, Hibernia's champions raid Raumarik, and Midgard's heroes win through their great quests.

events.text: The conflict between Albion, Midgard and Hibernia began with the power vacuum left by King Arthur's death.
Midgard's great quests send healers and shamans after Loken, hunters and shadowblades after Oona, and the mystics after Kelic.
Each frontier has an old giant who belongs to no realm: a green knight, the Glacier Giant and Evern.

eras.name: The Shrouded Isles
eras.summary: A Troll Father walks into Jordheim: the morvalt have overrun Aegir. Midgard sails with the Valkyn to reclaim Trollheim and meets the rime giants, the old one of the Iarnwood and the morvalt's dig for their Mother.

events.text: A lone Troll Father came to Jordheim: the morvalt had swept Aegir and Trollheim held out only for a time; the tamed Valkyn joined Midgard to cleanse the island.
The morvalt broke Faraheim's rockwall to reach Modernagrav, seeking the Mother, and found an ancient skeleton guarded by the dead.
When Aegir rose out of the mist, Tuscaran Glacier, Trollheim and Iarnvidiur's Lair became Midgard's greatest dungeons.

eras.name: The Present Day
eras.summary: The present age: the realm raids the old places, the Herald records the kills, and the dead of every era still wait for an answer.

events.text: The realm raids each great place with as many as the old accounts say it took.
A band of dwarves seeking to strengthen Midgard found the frostalfs, who agreed to fight beside the realm, knowing their fate was still bound to it.
events.source: http://www.camelotherald.com/more/1131.shtml (Camelot Herald, 2003-10-23, 'Trials of Atlantis, an Overview'; Wayback capture 2005-12-26)

events.text: The harbour talk says that in each realm the leaders and chosen others had the same dream of a strange land where heroes are tried against fantastic creatures, and a voice promising them power there. Some call it the gods' doing, some magic, some an enemy's trick. The sailors of Aegirhamn swear the island remnants of Atlantis lie somewhere in the encircling seas and that the other two realms dreamed it too; nobody has sailed there and come back to prove it.
events.source: http://www.camelotherald.com/more/1131.shtml (Camelot Herald, 2003-10-23, 'Trials of Atlantis, an Overview'; Wayback capture 2005-12-26)

factions.name: The Hrimthursa
factions.summary: The rime giants of Tuscaran Glacier: Queen Kula and King Tuscar, a Council that argued for peace and Icelords who wanted war.

factions.name: The Troll Fathers
factions.summary: The ancient precursors of trolls and kobolds who built Trollheim and fled deeper when it fell.

factions.name: The Valkyn
factions.summary: Morvalt tamed by the Troll Fathers, who took a Norse god and joined Midgard.

factions.name: The Morvalt
factions.summary: Prehistoric savages who overran Aegir and hold Trollheim; the crazed ones dig for their Mother on Modernagrav.

factions.name: The Wolf's Brood
factions.summary: Gjalpinulva the Fenris wolf's daughter, her drakulv and her firstborn Yar; and, by the grandmothers' tale, the wolves of the Iron Wood.

factions.name: The Servants of Iarnvidiur
factions.summary: The old one of the Iarnwood and everything in her lair: her wolves, her herd of animus, her plague.

factions.name: The Iarn Dwarves
factions.summary: The free dwarf clans of Aegir: the Remnants of Faraheim with their griffons, and Chief Tarek's people under the iron trees.

factions.name: The Svartalfar
factions.summary: Dark elves: thralls of the arachites in Spindelhalla, dragon-watchers of Svarhamr in Malmohus.
factions.text: Their oldest grief is the quarrel of the twin princes Hauk and Enar, set on by a treacherous human stranger who left with the kingdom's treasures; Hauk went down into Niflheim, and his descendants, the frostalfs, came back to Midgard's side only lately. Svartalf scouts were the first to tell Midgard what lives in Malmohus.

factions.name: The Skogsra
factions.summary: Forest folk of Faraheim who lead travellers astray, the Shade Seekers among them.

factions.name: The Tradklan
factions.summary: A small, loud tree-clan of Faraheim led by Cronk.

factions.name: Beasts of the Wild
factions.summary: Great beasts who serve no one: griffons on the glacier, render packs and terror birds in Faraheim, the old fish of Mahattava's lake.

factions.name: Loki's Mischief
factions.summary: What gets out when the venom bowl spills: Loken in Raumarik, and the jotuns who do the bound god's work, like Ulfketill.

factions.name: The Jotuns of Vanern
factions.summary: Swamp giants who build in clay and still try to better the clay giant of the old tale.

factions.name: The Dishonoured Dead
factions.summary: The dead the valkyries passed by: the Cursed Tomb's draugr, Raumarik's deserters and curses, the Wretch of Winter, the Revenant's fortress.

factions.name: The Bound of Dodens Gruva
factions.summary: Jarl Ormarr's miners, huscarls and household, bound by Aros the Spiritmaster so the calling below could not have them.

factions.name: The Summoners
factions.summary: The Grand Summoner Govannon and his three summoners, who call the dead of every realm in the hall under the three frontiers (shared with Albion and Hibernia).

factions.name: The Lords of the Undead
factions.summary: The faction of the Summoner's Hall's dead, the answerers of the calling (Allakhazam: the hall's mobs are on Lords of the Undead).

factions.name: The Sidhe of the Hall
factions.summary: Sidhe magickers, protectors and a high lord who serve the summoners as if they had forgotten whose they are (shared).

factions.name: The Werewolves
factions.summary: The varulv of Skona and the court of King Hresvelgr in Varulvhamn, with the old wolfaur.

factions.name: The Arachites
factions.summary: Spider-folk of Spindelhalla who farm silk with svartalf thralls and pray to something in the deep.

factions.name: The Tomte
factions.summary: House-spirits driven underground by forgotten butter, led by Nisse.

factions.name: The Vendo
factions.summary: A hairy, howling people of the caves north of Mularn, with their goblins.

factions.name: Hibernia's Champions
factions.summary: Hibernians who carry the war into Midgard's own wilds, like Oona at Raumarik's river fork.

factions.name: The Frontier Giants
factions.summary: The old giants who belong to no realm and stand on the frontiers; Midgard's is the Glacier Giant.

factions.name: The Hagbui
factions.summary: The mound-dwellers of Vanern: a jarl's dead household that never left its barrows, with its thanes, runemasters, heralds and a forge that still burns.

factions.name: The Giants of Raumarik
factions.summary: Hugi and the frost cyclopes of Raumarik's south-west, with the frost stallions that run for them.

factions.name: The Dark Seithkona
factions.summary: Seeresses who followed Ydenia out of the Seithkona Circle into Vanern Swamp, and still keep her high seat.

factions.name: The Realms' Enemies
factions.summary: Albion and Hibernia on Midgard's frontier: the war for the keeps, the ghosts of invaders who died in Uppland's snow, and the Albion men in the Jamtland hills who buy the Red Daggers' roads.

factions.name: The People of Dellingstad
factions.summary: The crater town of Delling: miners, fortifiers, soothsayers and crossbowmen who trade on their own terms and treat strangers, even Midgard's, as enemies until proved friends.

factions.name: The Houses of the Gods
factions.summary: Midgard's callings as houses of its gods, with their gothi and gythjur in Jordheim's two temple halls (the Aesir's: Odin, Thor, Tyr, Modi, Bragi, Eir; the eastern: Hel, Ymir, Loki, Skadi), Kelgor's and Bodgar's houses that came with the Valkyn, the trainers who teach their young, and the jarls of the high hall who keep the realm's names and vault.

factions.name: The Hidden People
factions.summary: The huldu of the Vale of Mularn and the Svealands, fair from the front and hollow behind, who lived beside the first farms unseen and stopped hiding when the farms stopped leaving things out for them.

factions.name: Clan Smyg
factions.summary: The hobgoblins of the Vale of Mularn under Smyga, named for sneaking, who raid between Mularn and Haggerfel; Carr left them.

factions.name: The Dark Pack
factions.summary: The sveawolves of the Svealands, who raise their young in the open fields while their mothers run the coasts: Morra on East Svealand's shore and Modervarg, the mother wolf of West Svealand.

factions.name: The Clan-Folk of Aegir
factions.summary: The small clan-folk of the Shrouded Isles who are not the tree-clan: the musslaklan of Aegir's Landing's west shore, the skalklan who dispute it with them, and the bergklan of the Gripklosa range. They trade with those the clan has taken in and fight everyone else.

factions.name: The Sjoalf
factions.summary: The sea-elves of the Shrouded Isles' waters, pale and long-fingered, whose cult in Munin Sound and Modernagrav prays to something in the deep with sacrificers, purifiers and four dream-sending stones.

factions.name: The Blodfelag
factions.summary: The blood-fellowship of West Svealand: huscarls, drengs and farmers who swore to each other in their own blood and wolves' blood instead of to a jarl, and keep a fort, witches, warhounds and captives for an oath nobody remembers the purpose of; their agents reach the frontier at Odin's Gate.

factions.name: The Fire of Muspelheim
factions.summary: What lives in the fire beyond Fort Veldon's pass: the fire giants who came to warm themselves, the raukomaz of the lava and their lord, the fire wyrms and cinder drakes, and the dverge who chose the heat for their forge, where the Grenlock crest is made whole.

factions.name: The Elements of the Caldera
factions.summary: The living stones and vapours of Delling's crater floor: golems of pumice, basalt and obsidian, steam and vapour elements, and the three golems who keep the keys to the dwarven king's box.

factions.name: The Deep Ones
factions.summary: What holds the deep roads under Spindelhalla's farm: the cave trows and their chief, the deeplurks, and the two old things at the bottom the svartalfar name for evil and dread.

factions.name: Sigurd, slayer of Fafnir
factions.summary: Sigmund's son, who reforged his father's sword, dug the pit under the dragon Fafnir and learned from the dragon's blood what the gold would do to him.
factions.text: Every jarl's hall in Midgard keeps a place for Sigurd the dragon-slayer, because he is the one whom the songs trust to know what a dragon costs. He was the son of Sigmund the Volsung, born after his father fell, and the skalds still sing of the Volsungs before him: how Sigmund and his son Sinfjötli ran the forests in wolf-skins they could not take off for ten days at a time, and how Sinfjötli died of a horn of poison his stepmother gave him. Sigurd was raised by the smith Regin, who hated his own brother Fafnir for the gold that Fafnir turned into a dragon to guard. From the shards of his father's sword Regin forged Gram, and Gram split Regin's anvil in two. On the road to Fafnir's heath, an old man with one eye told Sigurd to dig more than one pit, because the dragon's blood would drown a man in a single trench. Sigurd lay in the pit under the path and drove Gram up into the dragon as it crawled over him. Fafnir spoke as it died, and warned him that the gold carried a curse. Sigurd roasted the heart for Regin, burned his thumb, and tasting the blood understood the speech of birds, who told him that Regin meant to kill him. He killed Regin, took the hoard and rode up to the mountain Hindarfell, where a ring of fire held the sleeping Valkyrie Brynhild. The skalds finish the tale where the dragon did: the gold killed everyone who touched it.

factions.name: Ragnar Lodbrok, who sang in the pit
factions.summary: The raider-king of the sagas, who won his queen by killing the serpent coiled around her bower and died singing in a pit of adders.
factions.text: The skalds of Midgard sing Ragnar Lodbrok as the king who laughed at his own death. He won his name, Hairy-Breeches, before he won his crown: Jarl Herraud of Gautland had a daughter, Thora, whose bower was ringed by a lindworm that had grown from a gift in a box until it circled the house, and Ragnar wore a cloak and trousers of shaggy hide, tarred and rolled in sand, and killed it. He took Thora for his wife, and after her Aslaug, the daughter of Sigurd and Brynhild, raised as a peasant girl and famous for her wit, whose sons Ivar the Boneless, Björn Ironside and Sigurd Snake-in-the-Eye fought across the western seas. Ragnar himself sailed to Northumbria with two ships and too few men, was taken by King Aella and thrown into a pit of vipers. The saga gives him the words every Midgard warrior knows from the pit itself: that the little pigs would grunt if they knew how the old boar suffered. His death-song, the Krakumal, gives the rest: a list of the battles he fought, the ale that waits in Odin's hall in curved horns, and the promise that he would die laughing. He died laughing. His sons came back for Aella with a great army, and the saga of that vengeance is the one every young raider asks to hear. It begins with the news. The messengers found the brothers each at his own work, the saga says, and each took it his own way: Björn was holding a spear, and gripped the shaft so hard that the wood kept the print of his hand; Hvitserk was at the board, and squeezed a playing-piece until the blood started from under his nails; the brother called Snake-in-the-Eye was paring his nails with a knife, and cut to the bone without feeling it. Ivar, who could not walk and was carried on a litter of poles, asked only how his father had died, and asked again, and changed colour as he listened. Then he went to Aella, not with an army but with a request: as much land as an ox-hide would cover. He cut the hide into a thread so fine that it went round ground enough for a stronghold, and from that stronghold he won Aella's own men away with gifts, and when his brothers came with their army Aella had few left to stand with him. The saga says they carved the eagle on his back. The skalds of Midgard sing the four brothers in the order the news found them, the spear, the board, the knife and the question, and say that a young raider who asks for the song should be told afterwards which brother he is.

factions.name: Hervor, who woke the dead for a sword
factions.summary: The shield-maiden of the sagas, who went to her father's burial mound at dusk and made him give her the cursed sword Tyrfing.
factions.text: Of the three heroes the songs of Midgard keep, Hervor is the one with the least to prove and the most to take. She was the daughter of Angantyr, one of the twelve berserk sons of Arngrim, who were killed on the island of Samsey by the Swedish champion Hjalmar the Brave and his sworn brother Orvar-Odd, though Hjalmar died there too of the wounds Tyrfing gave him, and she grew up hearing that her father's sword, Tyrfing, lay in his barrow with him. She put on a man's clothes, took the name Hervard, and went to the island alone as the sun set, and walked through the fires that ring the barrows at night, past the shepherds who ran from her. At the mound she called her father, who answered from the grave and told her to leave the sword: it would kill a man each time it was drawn, would never miss, and would destroy her own kin. She told him that she would take it, and that she would lay a curse on all the barrow-dead, that they would rot in their mounds, if he refused. He gave it to her, and warned her again. She went back to the ships with the sword, and the saga of her son Heidrek is the story of what the sword did.
